title: Rollback guard and sticky health gates for controlled cold-drain hotfix
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Introduce a rollback-safety guard and sticky health gates to avoid cascading evictions during controlled cold-drain and emergency rollbacks. Improves stability of regional failover and reduces SLO blips during maintenance.
description:
Context: During a recent maintenance window (INC-2025-11-12) we observed a cascading eviction pattern when a partial region cold-drain was initiated and then a rollback occurred while nodes were still transitioning. The quick sequence of drain -> rollback -> rejoin caused a flood of health transitions that tripped circuit heuristics and produced a multi-tenanted degradation event.

Motivation: Add a lightweight guard that (1) prevents immediate full rejoin/flapping after a rollback, (2) surfaces a sticky health gate so control-plane decisions can respect transient state for a short cooldown, and (3) emits structured telemetry so incident responders can diagnose propagation windows. This is a hotfix intended to ship quickly and then be iterated.

What this PR does (summary):
- Add RollbackGuard service (control-plane) which marks a node/slot as "recently-rolled-back" for a configurable cooldown window. This state is consulted by eviction, circuit, and routing subsystems.
- Introduce StickyHealthGate annotation on node heartbeat messages and KV-control metadata. The gate prevents immediate aggressive preemption/eviction for up to N seconds after a rollback or forced-restart.
- Emit structured telemetry events (rb_guard.event, sticky_gate.transition) to the observability pipeline (OTLP) with low-cardinality tags for tenant/region/node-role.
- Fast-path checks in the scheduler and SLO enforcer to treat nodes with sticky gates as "stabilizing" (reduce eviction priority, avoid aggressive tenant migration).
- Add a rollback-safe drain orchestration mode for the cluster-agent that stages operations to avoid synchronized mass rejoin windows.

Files changed (high-level):
- controlplane/rollback_guard/ (new) - core guard service + RPCs
- controlplane/heartbeat/annotator.go - add StickyHealthGate value + serialization
- scheduler/eviction_policy.go - consult rollback guard + lower eviction weight
- enforcer/slo_enforcer.go - treat sticky gates as stabilization signals for N seconds
- agent/drain_orchestrator.go - new staged-drain mode and recovery hooks
- telemetry/emitters/otlp.go - new events and batching logic
- tests/integration/rollback_guard_test.go - added test harness covering rollback->rejoin scenarios

Commits (summary):
- 0f3b2c1  add RollbackGuard skeleton and API
- 4a9d7e0  annotate heartbeats with StickyHealthGate
- f1b2c88  enforcer: treat sticky nodes as low-priority for eviction
- b6e4a3d  drain_orchestrator: add staged cold-drain flow and safepoints
- cadf9a0  telemetry: emit rb_guard.event and sticky_gate.transition
- e2d11f7  integration tests and flake fixes

Testing and validation performed:
- Unit tests for RollbackGuard state machine and cooldown arithmetic.
- Integration test that simulates 1000-node cold-drain with an immediate rollback; verified no cascading tenant evictions in 25/25 runs.
- Local perf run to ensure telemetry batching cost is negligible (avg 4% CPU increase in control-plane under synthetic load).
- Manual canary: deployed to staging region eu-west-2 and executed staged-drain followed by rollback twice; observed expected sticky_gate transitions and reduced eviction churn.

Rollout plan:
1) Deploy control-plane RollbackGuard as a feature-flagged service to host-primary (flag default=off). 2) Enable flag for staging and run 24h soak. 3) Toggle for a small production cohort (10% traffic across one region). 4) Monitor rb_guard.event rate, eviction counts, and tenant error budget. 5) Ramp to 100% if no regressions.

Rollback plan (emergency):
- Flip feature-flag off to stop consulting guard (fast). If necessary, revert commit b6e4a3d which introduces staged-drain orchestration.

Operational notes:
- Default sticky cooldown: 120s (configurable via rollout config). Shorter values (30s) caused a small uptick in tenant migration in canary; longer values (>300s) delayed necessary preemption under overload.
- Telemetry uses low-cardinality tags (region, node_role, tenant_bucket) to prevent high-cardinality explosion.
- This PR does not change any customer-facing API, and no schema migration is required.

References:
- Linear ENG-1897: Postmortem follow-up: rollback-induced cascade
- Incident INC-2025-11-12: partial-region cold-drain degradation

Checklist:
- [x] Unit tests
- [x] Integration tests
- [x] Canary validated in staging
- [x] Observability dashboards updated (rb_guard panel)
- [x] Rollout plan documented

Merging notes: squash-and-merge; include a short changelog entry referencing ENG-1897 and the incident.

review_thread: Priya Natarajan (2025-11-18): This looks good overall. Can you clarify the cooldown default and where it's documented?
Maya Chen (2025-11-18): Default is 120s; added note in description and added config option in controlplane/config.go. Will update docs once canary is green.

Liam O'Connor (2025-11-19): Concern: sticky gates might mask real host failures. Please ensure we still surface critical health states to SRE alerts. Suggested adding an override to force immediate eviction for critical hardware signals.
Maya Chen (2025-11-19): Added the override hook in scheduler/eviction_policy.go and a unit test asserting critical signals bypass sticky gate. Kept gate only for soft-rejoins/rollback flows.

Diego Romano (2025-11-19): Integration tests look solid. One nits: telemetry tag names are slightly different than the backend expectation (rb_guard vs rollback_guard). I changed emitter to rb_guard.event as a compromise and noted mapping in observability README.
Priya Natarajan (2025-11-20): Approved after canary results. +1 to merge as hotfix.
